HirError::SharedMissingBarrierBeforeCrossInvocationRead for the decidable same-block no-back-edge straight-line case (zero false positives, the canonical NVIDIA-passes/AMD-races trap). Reuses the EXISTING divergent_context_depth (typecheck.rs:545; incremented at lines 956-967 for if/else and 1174-1176 for loops). oq1_oq2_adoption_confirmed.feasibility: Both checks are provably feasible: OQ1 is a forward linear scan within one basic block; OQ2 reuses existing depth-counting infrastructure with one additional guard condition. Neither requires new dataflow analysis.

strengths: Scope discipline is exceptional: the FA2 relabel is thorough and the C1/C2 staging rationale is compelling (C1 provides the bit-exact baseline for @equiv_fp_tol verification of C2's streaming arithmetic — textbook anti-reward-hacking).

The CRITICAL-2 self-audit found 4 additional hardcoded-version sites the pessimistic reviewer missed (metadata.rs:276, :288, :334, :340-355), demonstrating a genuine codebase read. The at_1553 reject-v3 inversion (site (e)) is identified as the most dangerous missed one — correct prioritization.

The shared-source coopmat emit separation (CRITICAL-3) is cleanly specified: separate functions, no storage-class flag added to the Buffer path, CoopMatLoadSource additive enum with Buffer as the default, and the stride-in-elements vs SSBO-row-stride distinction explicitly called out in both the spec and coder_handoff_notes.

AT-1622 hardening correctly addresses the M3.1.5 anti-lesson: the genuineness test now requires different K-loop trip-count AND bit-exact GPU results for both tile_k values, not just different array sizes. Size-diff alone is insufficient — this insight is explicitly captured.

Cross-vendor race honesty is fully adopted and accurately bounded: AT-1606 proves only (i) bit-exact WITH barrier and (ii) diagnostic emission; the OQ1 hard error is labeled the real protection; EB.1 (AMD/Intel) is the untested gap. The design does not overclaim.
26 acceptance tests in the M3.2 range (AT-1600..AT-1635), each with specific expected_behavior and verified_via. The test structure is complete and honest about hardware gating.

The dedup rule for shared arrays (distinct OpTypeArray+OpVariable per SharedId, shared elem-ptr type per elem ScalarTy) is technically correct per the SPIR-V type-caching model and is guarded by AT-1615.

Workgroup StorageClass capability minimality is correctly specified: no new capability or extension, f16/i8/i16/i64/f64 pull only type capabilities (NOT StorageBuffer8/16BitAccess KHR extensions which gate StorageBuffer only). This is a subtle but critical distinction confirmed by the SPIR-V and Vulkan specs.
SPIR-V 1.3 OpEntryPoint interface exclusion of Workgroup vars is correct and the forward-compat note for SPIR-V 1.4+ is appreciated.
concerns: Minor: AT-1623 (resident benchmark) gates correctness on 'presence + correctness, not a hardcoded threshold.' The no-per-iter-allocation guarantee is stated in the AT description and coder_handoff_notes. This is sufficient for the design phase; the Coder must confirm by inspecting the dispatch-N loop. Not blocking.

Minor: The tiled_attention.axc (C1) Lavapipe + NVIDIA dual-path note in PART C1 says it 'runs on Lavapipe (scalar f16->f32 dot products, no coopmat).' The Lavapipe f16->f32 promotion for scalar ops is a Mesa llvmpipe behavior; confirm at Coder time that the f16 SSBO loads don't require a Float16 capability that Lavapipe's SPIR-V translator rejects. This is an implementation-time concern, not a design blocker. AT-1630 covers the full GPU path.

Minor: The 'all-invocations-enter loop body is uniform' rule for OQ2 is correct as a conservative approximation for the M3.2 shipped kernels (the K-loop trip count is workgroup-uniform). If a future kernel has a loop with a data-dependent trip count per-invocation, OQ2 would miss a divergent barrier in that loop body. This is acceptable as a known limitation documented in technical_spec A.4.2 and does not affect M3.2 correctness.
validation_against_existing: workgroup_barrier() reuse is verified against actual codebase: codegen/src/subgroup.rs:34,298-300 emits OpControlBarrier scope=Workgroup(2)/Workgroup(2)/semantics=0x108 (AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory); test lines 517-519 assert the scope/semantics values. Single-barrier sufficiency for the straight-line stage->barrier->read pattern and dual-barrier requirement for the K-loop WAR are both correct per the Vulkan Memory Model.

The single-index vs two-index access-chain distinction mirrors the actual buffer implementation: buffers.rs:111 wraps the runtime array in OpTypeStruct (confirmed by the Architect's CRITICAL-3 codebase verification), requiring a leading zero_id for member-0 selection. A Workgroup OpTypeArray has no struct wrapper, so a single index is not only correct but required by spirv-val.
CoopMatLoadSource additive-enum pattern mirrors the existing CoopMatShapeMeta additive field from M3.1 — proven pattern for back-compat.

The metadata SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS allowed-set pattern mirrors explicit version lists used in mature SPIR-V toolchains (e.g. IREE's module_utils.cc: 'kSupportedVersions' list for ABI back-compat) — a proven approach over range checks.

The divergent_context_depth reuse (OQ2) mirrors validate.rs:189's SubgroupOpInDivergentContext warning that already uses the same depth. Extending it to workgroup_barrier is consistent with the existing architecture.

Rust-GPU (gfx-rs/rust-gpu): emits Workgroup OpVariables as global module-scope variables (not Function-block locals), consistent with the spec's global-variable scoping rule. The AXIOM-Compute spec mirrors this pattern (emit_shared_globals before begin_block).
external_references: SPIR-V Unified Specification §3.32.6 (OpTypeArray): 'Length must be the <id> of a constant instruction of scalar integer type. It specifies the number of elements in the array.' — confirms OpConstant id, not a literal.
SPIR-V Unified Specification §3.32.14 (OpAccessChain): 'Indexes walk the type hierarchy' — a flat OpTypeArray needs exactly one index operand; spirv-val enforces this.
SPIR-V Unified Specification §3.47 Storage Class: Workgroup requires Shader capability only — no extension. Int8/Float16/etc. type capabilities are separate.

SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix (Khronos): 'The Pointer operand to OpCooperativeMatrixLoadKHR may be a pointer of any storage class supported by the implementation, including Workgroup.' — validates the shared-source coopmat load.
Vulkan spec §10.2.3 VkPhysicalDeviceLimits: maxComputeSharedMemorySize (mandatory limit, present on all Vulkan 1.0+ devices) — validates the preflight design.

VK_KHR_8bit_storage / VK_KHR_16bit_storage: these extensions gate StorageBuffer and (optionally) UniformConstant/Input/Output storage classes only — Workgroup storage requires only the type-level Int8/Float16 capability, NOT these extensions. Confirmed by VK_KHR_8bit_storage spec §1.

Vulkan Memory Model spec §4: OpControlBarrier with Workgroup scope and AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory semantics is the correct synchronization primitive for cross-invocation shared-memory visibility within a workgroup — exactly what subgroup.rs:298-300 emits.

Dao et al. 'FlashAttention-2' (2023) arXiv:2307.08691: online softmax (running m_i, l_i, output rescaling) is the defining contribution — C1's full two-pass softmax is correct and useful but is not FA2 by any definition.

SPIR-V 1.3 spec §2.16.1 (OpEntryPoint interface): 'The interface operands are the <id>s of all global variables in Input and Output Storage Classes' — Workgroup vars correctly excluded. SPIR-V 1.4 changed this to all global vars — the forward-compat note in the spec is appropriate.

Rust-GPU (gfx-rs/rust-gpu) source: global Workgroup variables emitted in the module's types_global_values section, not as Function-block OpVariables — consistent with AXIOM-Compute's emit_shared_globals before begin_block.
